run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log level and re-run the query.

report.summary: The requested term query on field `level` returned zero hits, and the reason is structural: index `app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d` has no `level` field. Its mapping defines only `@timestamp` (date), `message` (text), `service` (keyword) and `severity` (keyword), so `level` is an unmapped field. Re-running the same term query against the mapped field `severity` returned 10 hits over the full authorized window 2026-11-20T03:35:22Z–2026-11-21T03:35:22Z. All 10 hits belong to service `checkout-275`, occur in a single 10-second burst from 2026-11-21T03:31:01Z to 03:31:10Z, and carry messages 'DB connection refused 1' through 'DB connection refused 10'. The index holds 30 documents in the window (INFO 15, ERROR 10, WARN 5), all with @timestamp in the 03:00–04:00Z hour of 2026-11-21. Only the log count is established here; the underlying DB-connectivity cause is a hypothesis that the log text alone supports but does not prove.

claims.text: Index `app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d` exists, is open and green, and reports docs.count 30 / store.size 10.1kb at the time of the query.
The mapping of `app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d` defines exactly four properties: `@timestamp` (date), `message` (text), `service` (keyword) and `severity` (keyword); no field named `level` is mapped.

The requested query `{"term":{"level":"ERROR"}}` returned total 0 hits (`relation: eq`) across the full authorized window 2026-11-20T03:35:22Z–2026-11-21T03:35:22Z, with 0 shard failures and timed_out false.

The query `{"term":{"severity":"ERROR"}}` returned total 10 hits (`relation: eq`) over the same full window, all from service `checkout-275` (single terms bucket doc_count 10), with timed_out false and 0 failed shards.

The 10 ERROR documents are timestamped 2026-11-21T03:31:01Z through 2026-11-21T03:31:10Z (one per second) and their messages read 'DB connection refused 1' … 'DB connection refused 10', each with service `checkout-275` and severity `ERROR`.
Across all 30 documents in the window, the `severity` distribution is INFO 15, ERROR 10, WARN 5, and every document falls in the single date_histogram bucket 2026-11-21T03:00:00Z (1h interval).
The requested query evaluated only over the tool's default 1-hour window (2026-11-21T02:35:22Z–03:35:22Z) also returned 0 hits for `term: {level: "ERROR"}`, matching the full-window result.

The zero count for `level` is explained by field naming, not by absence of errors: `level` is not in the index mapping, whereas `severity` is the mapped keyword field for log level and yields the 10 ERROR hits.

The error text 'DB connection refused' in the checkout-275 logs suggests a database dependency refused connections around 2026-11-21T03:31Z, but the logs do not name the database endpoint, and no trace, pod or config evidence was examined in this Run to confirm it.

Query `severity` (value `ERROR`) rather than `level` for this index, and if broader level coverage is needed, add a `level`→`severity` field alias via an index mapping change; alias changes were not made in this read-only Run.

gaps: The database or endpoint that 'DB connection refused' refers to is not identified by any field in these documents; no service, pod, configmap or trace evidence was inspected to name it.
Only 30 documents exist in this index, and all carry @timestamp inside 2026-11-21T03:00–03:35Z; log data outside that hour, and any retention or ingest gaps, are unknown.
Whether the 10 ERROR lines reflect a persistent or transient DB outage beyond 03:31:01–03:31:10Z is unknown; no later logs exist in this index within the authorized window.
No change_history integration is available in this Run, so whether a configuration or deployment change preceded the 03:31Z error burst could not be checked.
next_steps: Inspect checkout-275 (Deployment/Pod) status, container restart reasons and events, plus any DB connection settings in its ConfigMap, to identify the refused database endpoint.
Check traces for the `checkout` service around 2026-11-21T03:31Z for failed downstream/DB spans to correlate the log burst with trace status codes.
If `level`-style queries are expected by other tooling, verify whether log shippers or dashboards should reference `severity` instead.
